notes.title: Update 6 : New Achievements, Weapon, and Boss!
notes.content:
Hello Survival Typists!

We’re back with another update packed with content, balance tweaks, and quality-of-life improvements. Let’s jump right into it!


New Weapon: Orbiter
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/2408213a03f42da41abd44494be99ad011eed0e0.gif"]

The Orbiter brings a fresh twist to the battlefield. When you type words starting with specific letters, it spawns orbs that rotate around your main weapon, dealing chemical damage to everything they pass through. Evolve it to deal electric damage, send out twin orbs in opposite directions, or form a damaging tether between the main weapon and the orb for some truly chaotic typing action.


New Boss: Gemini
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/01e59071ce4220b91476486d230916e9d455dbc1.gif"]

The Gemini isn’t a single boss. It’s two. Damaging only one won’t get you far, because they constantly heal each other to the highest health between them. You’ll need to split your focus and keep your damage even. And when they unleash their Tendril attack? Get ready to mash your keys or buttons fast!


New Achievements
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/ca91811e8c6c9968ca4a66a4fdb20c8f752ff77d.gif"]

We heard your feedback. More achievements, please! This update adds a fresh batch, including simpler ones for new players and tough-as-nails challenges for our veteran typists. There’s something for everyone.


New Evolutions for Chopper
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/1883f717128e5f82ed098c7caaed483fec4c774e.gif"]

Chopper gets two new ways to shred:
Saw Launcher turns the Chopper into a barrage of smaller saw-blades.
Bloodbath adds bonus damage to bleeding enemies and raises their double damage drop chance.


New Audio Themes[previewyoutube="FxTeYlRQsdk;full"][/previewyoutube]
You can now groove to two new music sets: Sunset is a laid-back, beachy lounge track for mellow vibes. Midnight is a lo-fi, head-nodding beat for focused destruction. Both pair beautifully with their visual theme counterparts, and you can swap them in the settings anytime.


Less Grind, More Game
Let’s be honest. We let the economy get a bit out of hand. So we’re fixing that. Coin drops have been doubled across the board, and all main weapons now cost a flat 1000 coins to unlock. No more grind. Just more typing, more fun.


2 New Augment Codices
Electric and Heat Augment Codices are now available. These unlock even more creative and dangerous build possibilities. Perfect for chasing those new achievements and wreaking havoc with elemental synergies.



That’s it for this update, folks! We hope you enjoy the new weapons, bosses, tunes, and quality-of-life changes. As always, we’ll be back again in 2 months with even more content and features to keep your fingers flying.

notes.title: Glyphica : Update 5 Brings new weapon, boss, consumable loot and more!
notes.content:
Hello Survival Typists!

We’re back with our regular updates, creating more content for you to enjoy, as well as some cosmetic experiments. Let’s get right to it!

New Weapon : Guardian
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/e82a750f09dfde8ba44c3c9863e530be33e0cd22.gif
The Guardian is a self propelled persistent Drone that guards the main turret with melee orbiting heat attacks. While it is a very powerful automated weapon, you need to keep picking up fuel to keep it going!

New Boss : Jormungandr
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/03ba34a82d92c437ccb60aa8817681f34a3e0495.gif
Last update we drew from Greek mythology, this time we take a nod to Norse mythology. Jörmungandr was a mythological creature who supposedly encircled the world, biting its own tail. One of the signals that the end of the world is coming is when the serpent finally lets go of its tail to wreak havoc on the world. Our version of the serpent circles your main weapon menacingly while releasing single letter projectiles for you to shoot down. 

Consumable Loot
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/c68a037966a7f3143bb86603bcb016c7b5829d24.gif
We’ve added a new consumables system to the game to allow you to store items in an inventory and then use them at will by typing the corresponding word. For example, the “Warhead” consumable triggers a massive string of explosions to take out enemies close to the main weapon. Right now all consumables are obtained via the Loot system, but we’re working to expand this and create more consumables in future updates.

Cosmetic Updates
We’re slowly rolling out cosmetic updates like letting you change the music and color scheme to the game. This is more complex than we thought it would be, and we need more time to implement it fully. However, we did want to give you all a sneak peek of how it would work. In the audio settings, you can now choose between Glyphica’s current music set and the original music it launched with back in the 2024 Next Fest. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/e7635919d8e739626b7333606c5e00a42d682a9b.gif
In addition, we’ve added a couple of new color themes aside from our light and dark themes. We will slowly open this up so more players can take advantage of this and make their own color themes, but if you have any theme requests let us know!

Combo Weapon Evolutions
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/91f94d0ed1a12a2fded1d481f20b4148d7c44167.gif
We’ve added more weapon Evolutions to the Minefield to increase the variations of gameplay. But on top of that, we’re excited to add weapon evolutions that only happen if you are using two specific weapons. The Dirty Bomb evolution makes your mines shoot puddles of goo when they explode, but you can only use this evolution if you are using Splattershot as well. We want future combos like this to be a cool surprise for players, but we’re leaking this one for you all to enjoy.

Omen Update
There were players who didn't want the weapons kept from growing due to the Omen II penalty. We've updated the omen system and replaced the penalty with a new 9-letter wordlist.

Localized Achievements

Achievements are now localized so you can all challenge yourselves to be better typists!

Outro
That’s it for this update folks! We hope you enjoy this update, and we will be back again in 2 months to give you some fresh new content and features!

New Main Weapon : Splatter Shot
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/51cb1b9b66913f2493d8730e2052df2e795c980b.gif
Splatter Shot introduces a different weapon and play style for our survival typists. Spit out nasty goo at your enemies to slow them down and deal D.O.T. while your other weapons finish them off. Evolutions allow you to change the damage type according to your build preference or gives you options to expand the spread of the goo.

Weapon Evolutions…Evolved!

Like some of our other bosses, Cerberus has a final form that comes back to haunt you later in the game. But we’ll keep that a secret for now…

notes.content:
[previewyoutube=o00bxvrM0qs;full][/previewyoutube]
Hello Survival Typists! 

This update does bring long term improvements and additions to the game that improve the experience for both old and new players alike.  Statistics and Leaderboards were one of our roadmap promises, and they are the focus of our update this time!

Stat Tracking
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/2690c52a845bf9f53ef023e8477e10edba0f2fff.gif
We know that a lot of you like keeping track of your stats in the game and seeing how you are improving over time. For each main weapon, if you do an endless run, we will track your latest 10 playthroughs and track your WPM and accuracy. This is our first iteration of statistics in the game. So if you guys have more things that you would like to track, please do let us know in the comments!

Friend Leaderboards
While the game is not built for competitive play, we know that a lot of you wanted to see how you stack up against your friends. In the leaderboard we take different stats like the time survived and difficulty level to give you a score, which is then used to rank you.

Each leaderboard is unique to a main weapon, which gives you a chance to beat your friends depending on which weapon is your main. In future updates we plan to add global leaderboards as well.

Run Information
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/ec29d0959bc6fc32b665c158ffbf4d6846b254e6.gif
Previously during a run we only showed you weapon information. Due to popular demand, we have added more information for you to better strategize your present and future runs.

You can now select between different tabs in the Run Information screen to show which loot you’ve picked up and which augments you have selected for this Run. If there is any other information you want here, please let us know and we’ll work on adding them!

Performance Improvements
We've improved the UI updating loop to be much more efficient, which yielded overall performance gains throughout the game. Now that has been fixed and we’re expecting you to have a much smoother game experience overall!

Loot Rework
Our loot has been neglected for a long time and we did a major rebalancing of the items pickups to better fit the current game meta. Some loot has been nerfed, and some have had more gradations added to them to fill in some gaps.  

Options Menu Organization
Another relatively small but meaningful update is a reorganizing of our options menu into different tabs. Why is this meaningful? Because it’s an important and necessary step for adding things like custom color themes and fonts into the game!

Wiki Localization
We added an official wiki in one of our recent updates, and have now updated it with more localized content!

Future Plans
And that’s all for Update 3. We hope you enjoy these updates! In the meantime, we’ll get back to work and bring you another update at the end of next month.

Independent Wordlists

Hopefully this overall brings an improved typing experience for players of all skill levels.

We’ve also globally lowered the speed of the randomly fast enemies that pop up in the game, as well as making some spawning changes in the code that SHOULD prevent the sudden spawning of hordes of enemies all at the same time, which is not intended.

[previewyoutube=DCwo-PD3Aeg;full][/previewyoutube]
Hello Survival Typists! 

As promised we are bringing you the first of our planned monthly updates. Update 1 brings you Augmentations, a new weapon, and a host of other small additions and improvements.

But first, we want to thank everyone who has bought the game so far. Glyphica has sold over 17,000 copies so far, with an 85% positive rating. We appreciate all the feedback so far, both good and bad. Now, on the update!

Augmentations
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/d84c5db2a7ce1e44da6431c14911bf14fd15a550.gif
The main event is Augmentations! Our trials get super hard as you advance, so we built the Augmentations system to complement them. As you play the game, you’ll now be able to pick up coins, which you then use to buy augments that you equip at the start of a play session.

For example, if you are super confident with your perfect input, choose the Immaculate Augmentation to improve your Crit chance. On the other hand if you make mistakes a lot, choose Scapegoat to automatically sacrifice a drone instead of losing your perfect input streak.

This is only the first batch of augmentations, and more will be added over time.

Barrage
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/7f373b47f909fba9a89d3622c81bf4170e740ed2.gif
Update 1’s new main weapon is Barrage. Unleash a flurry of Robotech style missiles at your enemies to cause AoE damage. But it takes time to reload, so it will be a matter of skill and timing as to when you unleash your rockets. To unlock barrage you will need to have finished at least Omen 3 on one of the other main weapons.
Difficulty Settings

Easier Difficulties
We’ve been reading the reviews and discussion on the forums and on Discord, and we know that some of you have been struggling with the difficulty of the game! So we’ve created two modes to ease you into Glyphica until you’re ready to take on our trials. Omens will not unlock and Achievements will be disabled when playing in either mode.

Typist
Typist mode is the purest form of Glyphica. Type to shoot, and that’s it. No other weapons, no upgrades, no experience, just typing. Only basic drones will spawn, and while they will increase in word length they can be taken out with one shot. This is probably best for the person who wants to just practice their basic typing skills.

Relaxed
Relaxed mode is basically like our normal mode, but with 50% less enemies to deal with. This is best for the person who is more confident with their typing now and wants to practice engaging with what the full game has to offer.

Spaces and Punctuation
We initially removed the need to type punctuation and spaces for our Poet boss because during our playtests people we’re having a hard time with the game. But it turns out some of you really want a legitimate typing experience! So we went ahead and added an option to toggle spaces and punctuation (very original, I know) in the options menu.

Special Characters Fallback
A lot of you were having trouble with special characters like ë or é in the game. And some of you just plain hated having to type with accented letters! Since we are dealing with so many possible different keyboard configurations, we made the decision to simplify everyone’s lives by making the game default to the “base” letter while playing the game. So for example if you see an é and freak out, don’t worry just type e.

Music
[previewyoutube=VPILuoKTzIg;full][/previewyoutube]
Our talented sound partners at Imba Interactive are at it again, providing not only new sounds for the barrage weapons, but boss music as well! The Poet mixes classical music with a modern edge (think witcher + drum and bass), while the Cypher, as a sort of codebreaking kind of boss, takes its influence from morse code, of all things!

More Poetry
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/192b41e31f2b680b6f7853c1e54c1cb1d1bbd398.gif
We saw that some of you were getting bored of the Poet’s poetry (and we can’t blame you) so we’re slowly working on adding to his repertoire. Currently we’ve added some more poetry to the English, Spanish, and French versions. We are actually using public domain poetry for this, so if you have any suggestions for popular poetry in one of the languages that is in public domain, let us know!

That's it for now! We plan on another smaller update at the end of this month, so keep an eye out for that!

notes.title: Glyphica : Typing Survival Early Access Now Available!
notes.content:
Hello Survival Typists!

The big day is finally here! We are so excited to finally release the Early Access version of Glyphica : Typing Survival. We want to thank everyone who has given us feedback, especially our playtesters, without whom we would not have been able to fine tune the game. If you’re been playing the game for a while already, here’s a peek at what’s new for you.

Cypher Boss
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/9608e91c933be56a5ff72c176d80eefa943700bb.gif
The Cypher Boss scrambles the text of any enemy nearby!

Heat Ray Main Weapon
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/c3e4f6c2c863bd3784a621d0e2774b2b463e981d.gif
The Heat Ray is weaker than the repeater, but fires a steady stream of energy in one direction!

Roadmap
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/bdb2693d1e1bf929c844f89c8153425e4dbb80cb.png
Now It’s time to talk about our post Early Access plans and roadmap so you have a better idea of where we’re headed. Our goal with Early Access was to bring the game to you with the basic gameplay loop in as polished a form as possible, then take the next 6 months to refine the concept and add more content to the game. We plan to update the game once a month for the next 6 months, with the final update culmination in the 1.0 release. 

Glyphica started out as a small project and was always meant to have a small scope. While we are attuned to the demands of our players, we have to be honest that there are certain limitations to what we can do to expand the game. This will be a constant negotiation between you and us, and we will do our best to bring out as much as we can with this game. But without further ado, here is what we are fully committed to doing!

Augmentations
The simple augmentation system from our demo was ripped out, and a new, more flexible one designed to take its place. There wasn’t quite enough time to implement it in the game for Early Access, however, and so this will be our first big update.

We envision augmentations to be like Balatro’s jokers, and players’ favorite augmentations can be equipped to suit their playstyle.

New weapons, Turrets, and Tags every Month!
An expanded arsenal of weapons and turrets to play with is scheduled for nearly every month of post launch development, so you will always have something new to play with!

New Bosses and Enemies
With new weapons you need new targets! While bosses and enemies a little more difficult to and won’t come out at the same pace as weapons, we’ll always be thinking about new ways to making typing survival more difficult!

Game Modes
The game will come with a mission mode and endless mode, but on top of that we are looking into other game modes as well, possibly including a “pure” typing game mode where you see how long you can go without any upgrades or weapons.

Themes and Customization
Somewhat in line with custom wordlists, we plan on having themes for the game that change the mood of the game entirely. Do you want to play something a little more chill, or do you wanna rock out while you shoot down some pesky words, we got you!

Down the road we do want to give the player more control over customization like fonts, music and stuff like that as well, but this may be a separate addition from themes which are intended to change the entire look of the game.

Modding and Wordlists
We are slightly limited by what we can do with modding, but we know that a lot of you are clamoring to have your custom wordlists in the game. That’s something we will definitely aim to add the the game!

Advanced Languages
Glyphica started out using only the Roman Alphabet, but we know now that there is a huge swathe of players interested in the game. While our selection of languages using the Roman Alphabet is already quite wide, we plan on expanding this languages that use different scripts. We already talked a little bit how this is actually more difficult than it sounds for us, but we’re committed to getting as wide a reach as possible!

Statistics and Leaderboards
While Glyphica is not necessarily an educational tool, we want you to be able to track your progress and see how you are improving over time. And we also know that the real reason you want to get better is to show your friends that you are better than them, so some sort of leaderboard integration is also in our plans.

Conclusion
Those are our current plans for post launch, set down in roughly the order we plan on tackling them. We estimate that this work will take us around 6-7 months, and the intent is to keep the scope of the game relatively small so that we can commit wholeheartedly to fulfilling them. Depending on the success of the game we may expand the scope, however we will always keep you informed if that will be the case. 

Thanks again for joining us on this ride everyone, and happy typing to you all!

notes.title: Glyphica : Typing Survival Devlog 0 - Languages and Localization
notes.content:
Hello Survival Typists,

We know it’s been a while since our last update, but we wanted to make sure you know we are hard at work and some of the stuff we’re working on right now.

We will have a much deeper dive into the mechanics of the game in a future post, but for now we wanna talk about languages! That’s right, we’re adding more languages to Glyphica so that more survival typists can enjoy the game!

Japanese
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/6a46d2e4bfae2c26b9794cf7b81e78ac30891771.png
First off, a huge shout out to our Japanese fans. We’re really blown away by how well you have responded to the game, and shown us the possibilities of Glyphica in other languages. We added Japanese localization as kind of an experiment, and then when it took off we were in that weird position of “oh wow, they really like it! Oh no. Now we actually have to do a good job at it.”

With the success of Japanese in mind, we started thinking about other languages to localize to. You’d think Simplified Chinese would be the first target both because of reach and because XM actually speaks and reads Chinese, but there was a little problem…

Language Limitations
The game was designed with the English language and Roman alphabet in mind, and some key mechanics were defined by this. For example, our typical wordlist is 1300 words, but it’s not as simple as downloading a random wordlist from the internet because we use word length as a balancing tool. So for our wordlists we have 5 sets of words from 4 characters up to 8 characters in length. 

Some of our weapons are also triggered by words starting out with a specific letter. Again this is for balancing purposes. So for each set of say, 4 letter words, we need at least 10 words for each letter.

That seems reasonable when you have a phonetic alphabet of 26 letters, but how does that work when you have Chinese characters that, even in the simplified form, use around 8000 characters?

Japanese writing is equally or even more complicated, with its three sets of characters ranging from kanji descended from Chinese characters up to hiragana and katakana which are alphabets used for japanese words and foreign loan words. Our saving grace with Japanese is that because of their complicated writing system, japanese keyboard use has adapted such that entering romaji (roman alphabet letters) which are then converted to japanese syllabary is a common enough thing that we could piggy back on it. This led to our current form of the Japanese version of the game which uses romaji input.

It’s not perfect, as on top of having three systems of writing, there are different methods of writing Japanese in romaji, and most Japanese games that focus on typing adapt to how the player types. This was far too difficult for us to implement in the game so we have had to resort to choosing what the most popular method is, based on consultation with our Japanese players.

While China has pinyin script and Korea has its own alphabet, culturally neither of them uses the Latin Alphabet in a similar way as Japanese. We have experimented with Korean and when we brought the game to BICFest it seemed to be ok, so we’ll investigate that further.

We’re also somewhat limited by our font, which doesn’t have cyrillic, thai, or vietnamese versions of its characters, so languages that use those letters are off our list for the immediate future.

Our Target Languages
That leaves us with a limited set of languages to choose from, which use the Roman alphabet. In the end, we’ve decided on supporting the following languages for our Early Access launch:

 English
 Spanish
 LatAm Spanish
 Portuguese
 Brazilian Portuguese
 Italian
 German 
 French
 Turkish
 Japanese
 Polish
 Indonesian


These represent both the easiest languages we could find, those with what we feel are a significant enough market to do localization, and in the case of Indonesian, we're making a bet into a Southeast Asian language that is supported by Steam. 

[previewyoutube=qVCdjYtUT78;full][/previewyoutube]

In line with some other marketing efforts, I've been making some ASMR/Gameplay videos for Glyphica. And since I am learning spanish and have a Spanish keyboard lying around, I thought I would make another video showing off the Spanish localization right now, made by our localizer Valentín Sánchez.

Our demo now has Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, and Turkish in the demo so if you speak those languages please let us know how it is!

notes.title: Glyphica Early Access Announcement and Roadmap
notes.content:
Hello Survival Typists!

We hope you’re all enjoying your summer vacations and steam summer sale bargains! It’s been a while since we last updated you, so we wanted to share what is in store for Glyphica.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/170709a9e2076fe083f969b5ab9473d47fcce350.gif

But first, we’re so excited to announce that we have more than 30,000 wishlists already! Thanks so much to everyone who has wishlisted the game. We know that you are all excited to know what is happening next, so lets get right into it!

Demo Updates
First of all, we have decided that we will keep the demo up for the foreseeable future. The demo has been a great way to show off the potential of the game and convince people to wishlist it, so we want to keep it available to download for now.

However, maintaining a demo at the same time as working on additions to the release version of the game is taking its toll on our lead dev XM. So from this point forward, while the demo will still be occasionally patched with bug fixes, there will no longer be new content and mechanics added to it. Those additions will instead be added to our Early Access Release!

Early Access Roadmap
That’s right, Glyphica will soon be coming to Early Access! We want to keep the date under wraps for know so that we can make a bit of a marketing splash around it, but we can talk about the things that we are currently adding to the game to expand on what is currently in the demo:

Weapon Evolution
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44862715/b0470c8d168987be4271eb97a5aba1bff4c1081f.gif
Weapons now evolve into more powerful versions of themselves when you use them to destroy more enemies. You get to pick from two options every Evolution, with each path differentiated and becoming more extreme the further down the evolutionary ladd. For example, the Repeater can evolve to have its projectiles ricochet off its first target to hit three other enemies.

Mission Mode
While we will maintain the current endless mode, we are planning to make the Glyphica experience more self contained with pacing similar to other roguelites. Mission mode will consist of a run of roughly 7 tiers with 5 missions in each tier. You’ll be able to buy some loot in between tiers, but most importantly you will be able to save your game, so you can take some well needed breaks if you need to.

Better Augmentations
We’re reworking the Augmentations to have more significant upgrades that change how you play Glyphica. More Augments will become available in a skill-tree format over time as you unlock them via challenges.

More Main Turrets and Weapons

A larger variety of weapons will be available in-game and the damage types have been expanded to include Cold, Heat, Electric and Chemical weapons, each with their unique status effects and characteristics. Additional Main Turrets like the Heat Ray and Barrage (both of which have been hinted at in the main menu of the demo) can be unlocked via challenges and playtime.

Player status effects
We have some really incredible players in our discord server already, playing for incredible amounts of time. So obviously we need to make things  a little trickier for them by adding status effects that increase the challenge of late game. 

We will add effects like:

 Taking damage from mistypes
 Words being hidden until they are closer to you
much, much more!


We believe these additions will make the game a much more complete experience for our Early Access supporters, and it will be a solid base for us to create more content on top of that.

Thanks so much for all the support so far everyone! We are working hard to make a successful release out of Glyphica, and we’ll be back with more updates for you soon!

- Fixed "Precision" loot item giving 20% crit chance instead of 2% like stated in description.
- Fixed crash due to negative weights when randomizing loot.
- Fixed crash due to log file prevented from being saved by antivirus software or similar.
- Fixed icon of Blade Trap not reflecting actual Blade Trap.

Balancing
----------
- Added adaptive difficulty to provide a bit more challenge to better players.
- Nerfed Hunter duration upgrades from 20% to 10%.
- Nerfed Spectre damage upgrades from 20% to 15%.
- Nerfed Spectre duration upgrades from 20% to 10%.
- Removed double word in early game, now they only start spawning if you pick an upgrade that adds double word chance.
- Make longer word chance force 8-character words instead of just increasing word length by 2.

New Features
--------------
- Added Japanese localization and wordlist (experimental)
- Level up is now triggered by spacebar / right-stick-down so as not to disrupt typing flow.
- Added windowed / fullscreen option.
- If enemy is destroyed while typing its word, the word will remain until it is completed or there is a mistype. Weapons will trigger on word complete normally.
- Added pause menu.
- Escape key now also closes weapon details panel.
- Hide words when game is paused to prevent abuse.

notes.title: Visual Update
notes.content:
https://i.imgur.com/VJTtvw6.gif

After receiving a lot of feedback from Reddit, we've made some minor adjustments to the visuals of the game for better readability and clarity.

We've added a spot of color to enemies so you can easily tell them from the projectiles and power-ups, increased font sizes, and boosted contrast. You can turn off the colored enemies in the options if the original monochromatic look is more your style.

As usual, we're always listening to feedback, and we aim to do this even more when our demo is released in about a months time! Stay tuned!
